rules.statement: Code paths meant to behave the same way (parallel code paths, sibling modules, symmetric operations such as read/write, encode/decode, sync/async overloads) must handle validation, errors, edge cases and logging the same way.
rules.why: The maintainer counts any asymmetry between paths meant to be equivalent as a gap that leaves the capability delivered inconsistently.
rules.check: Compare each changed method with its siblings and counterparts. Flag one that validates an input, throws a particular exception, handles an edge case or logs an event while its counterpart doesn't.

rules.statement: When a change alters a type, member, behavior or contract, update every place that references it (callers, overloads, tests, XML docs, README and other docs) in the same change.
rules.why: Out-of-sync references create inconsistencies and contradictions between files; a change in one file has to stay consistent with every place it's referenced.
rules.check: For each renamed, re-signatured or behavior-changed item in the diff, look for callers, tests, doc comments and markdown that still describe the old name or behavior.

rules.statement: Don't duplicate logic across files or methods; route repeated behavior through one shared implementation so the copies can't drift apart.
rules.why: Duplicated logic tends to get out of sync, which leads to inconsistent behavior.
rules.check: Flag new code that re-implements validation, parsing, mapping or computation that already exists elsewhere in the change or codebase, especially where the copies already differ slightly.

rules.statement: A feature's implementation must cover its failure modes, edge cases, invariants and input validation all the way down to the low-level code, not just the happy path.
rules.why: A missing failure mode, edge case, invariant or validation leaves the capability incomplete, and closing it counts as part of the capability, not as new scope.
rules.check: Trace each capability in the diff into its low-level methods. Flag unvalidated inputs, unhandled null/empty/boundary values, swallowed or unhandled failures, and invariants that are assumed but never enforced.

rules.statement: Failure paths in a capability must have observability: log or report failures and significant rejections, the same way equivalent paths already do.
rules.why: The maintainer lists a missing observability/logging path as a gap that leaves the capability incompletely delivered.
rules.check: Look for catch blocks, rejection branches or early-return error paths in the diff that produce no log or telemetry, where similar paths elsewhere do.

rules.statement: Implemented behavior must match the intent described in the governing spec, design doc, ticket or README, and any low-level divergence from that intent must be fixed.
rules.why: The spec or docs are the source of intent, and comparing against them is how low-level gaps are found.
rules.check: Compare the changed behavior with the relevant RFC, spec, design doc or README. Flag missing required behaviors, wrong defaults or error semantics, and contradictions with the documented contract.

rules.statement: Tests for a changed capability must cover its edge cases and failure modes, not only the success path.
rules.why: The review explicitly checks tests for edge cases, and any edge case or failure mode left untested is a gap.
rules.check: For each new or changed branch, validation or error path in production code, check that a test exercises it. Flag test changes that only cover the happy path.

rules.statement: Give members and parameters names and semantics that state their meaning without ambiguity, and keep naming consistent with related members.
rules.why: The review looks for unclear semantics and naming inconsistencies.
rules.check: Flag names that are ambiguous, that contradict what the code does, or that use different terms for the same concept than sibling members do.
